newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Merrill Lynch buys 19 pct of Israel's Agis.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch buys 19 pct of Israel's Agis.

text.p: Merrill Lynch has purchased 19 percent of Israeli drug manufacturer Agis Industries Ltd for 200 million shekels ($58.57 million), Agis chairman and general manager Moshe Arkin said on Sunday.
The shares were purchased from the Arkin family, which controls Agis, for various clients of Merrill Lynch and not for one specific investor, Arkin said.
Merrill Lynch bought 5.5 million shares in an off-the-floor transaction at 36 shekels a share.
Agis shares, which have more than doubled since the end of August, are trading at 39.10 shekels.
The Arkin family, whose holdings will be reduced to 45 percent of Agis's issued share capital after the transaction, will net 180 million shekels, Arkin told Reuters.
Merrill Lynch will receive a transaction fee of 19.6 million shekels for acting in effect as underwriter for the deal, Arkin said.
Under Israeli law, the Arkin family will not have to pay tax on the proceeds from the sale, Arkin said.

He said the sale is part of an effort to internationalise trading in the company's shares. This effort could include a future offering of Agis shares on Nasdaq, though there are no definite plans yet for such a float, Arkin said.
Agis had sales of 702 million shekels and net profit of 48.3 million shekels in 1996. It controls Clay-Park Labs Inc, a U.S. generic private-label maker of topical products.
